excerpt_i18n.en: On August 19, Jefferies analysts tested eight mainstream global AI Agents on real office tasks. Results showed that through the synergy of model and Harness, Alibaba's Qwen Office ranked first in comprehensive score, surpassing US Agent tools such as Claude Cowork and Codex. The test included five real office tasks: summarizing annual reports based on multiple documents, searching and comparing company operating data online, operating a real desktop browser to complete information retrieval and document generation, creating English PPTs from data, and generating marketing posters based on reference images. Results showed Qwen Office performed in a relatively balanced manner overall, excelling particularly in complex office tasks, web browser control, and multimodal content generation, and was the only Agent product to score above 90 in all evaluation dimensions. The report further analyzed Agent capabilities by splitting them into model and Harness. The so-called Harness is a full set of engineering mechanisms running around the model, including instructions, context, tool calls, boundary control, feedback correction, and governance. According to Jefferies' calculations, Qwen Office's "implicit Harness score" ranked first among the tested products, higher than seven mainstream domestic and international Agent products including Claude Cowork and Codex. This also implies that beyond the underlying model, engineering and product capabilities matter.
